what: What is CSV on the Web?
title: Read and Write CSVW in R
text: W3C’s CSV Web Working Group produced series recommendations working tabular data web. Model Tabular Data Metadata Web describes annotate tables metadata, processing applications locate metadata parse annotated tables. Metadata Vocabulary Tabular Data provides specification annotating tables metadata various levels, groups tables relate individual cells within table. vocabulary provides mapping annotated tables can transform CSV formats: csv2json csv2rdf csvwr library implements parts standard R. overall goal project support reading writing annotated CSV tables, order ensure consistent processing reduce amount manual work needed parse prepare data can used analysis. Practically speaking, annotate csv file providing accompanying json document containing metadata. benefit annotating tables csvw benefit : csv dialect (.e. choice field separator quoting characters) explicitly defined, helping avoid parsing mistakes columns can given syntactically-valid variable names (retaining human-readable labels display) cell types declared, obviating need e.g. parse dates (figure-formatting strings) package includes example csv json explore. csv file: annotation:
code: library(csvwr)  compsci_csv <- csvwr_example("computer-scientists.csv")  cat(readLines(compsci_csv),sep="\n") #> Name,Date Of Birth #> Barbara Liskov,1939-11-07 #> Evelyn Boyd Granville,1924-05-01 #> Ada Lovelace,1815-12-10 compsci_json <- csvwr_example("computer-scientists.json")  cat(readLines(compsci_json),sep="\n") #> { #>   "@context": "http://www.w3.org/ns/csvw", #>   "tables": [{ #>     "url": "computer-scientists.csv", #>     "tableSchema": { #>       "columns": [{ #>         "name": "name", #>         "titles": "Name", #>         "datatype": "string", #>         "propertyUrl": "foaf:name" #>       }, { #>         "name": "dob", #>         "titles": "Date Of Birth", #>         "datatype": "date", #>         "propertyUrl": "schema:birthDate" #>       }], #>       "aboutUrl": "http://example.org/computer-scientsts/{#name}", #>       "primaryKey": "name" #>     } #>   }] #> }

what: How do I create CSVW table annotations?
title: Read and Write CSVW in R
text: can course write json metadata hand, already table data frame R can use get head start. provide derive_table_schema function data frame prepare table annotations. Notice column names, titles, datatypes derived data frame. can course refine schema wish (e.g. declare constraints datatypes add uri templates). can pass create_metadata build complete annotation. First build table description. requires provide URL csv can found. example, save data frame local file: can create table description using filename URL schema created earlier: Relative URLs like make sense json metadata csv table found place. may instead want unambiguously locate file absolute URL like https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Robsteranium/csvwr/master/inst/extdata/computer-scientists.csv work even metadata table held different locations. Now can build complete annotation: can serialised JSON: JSON may written disk:
code: d <- data.frame(x=c("a","b","c"), y=1:3) (s <- derive_table_schema(d)) #> $columns #>   name titles datatype #> 1    x      x   string #> 2    y      y  integer write.csv(d, "table.csv", row.names=FALSE) tb <- list(url="table.csv", tableSchema=s) (m <- create_metadata(tables=list(tb))) #> $`@context` #> [1] "http://www.w3.org/ns/csvw" #>  #> $tables #> $tables[[1]] #> $tables[[1]]$url #> [1] "table.csv" #>  #> $tables[[1]]$tableSchema #> $tables[[1]]$tableSchema$columns #>   name titles datatype #> 1    x      x   string #> 2    y      y  integer j <- jsonlite::toJSON(m) jsonlite::prettify(j) #> { #>     "@context": [ #>         "http://www.w3.org/ns/csvw" #>     ], #>     "tables": [ #>         { #>             "url": [ #>                 "table.csv" #>             ], #>             "tableSchema": { #>                 "columns": [ #>                     { #>                         "name": "x", #>                         "titles": "x", #>                         "datatype": "string" #>                     }, #>                     { #>                         "name": "y", #>                         "titles": "y", #>                         "datatype": "integer" #>                     } #>                 ] #>             } #>         } #>     ] #> } #> cat(j, file="metadata.json")
